item.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
item.description: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?

item.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
item.description: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.

item.title: Pasture mealybugs have killed off huge swaths of grasses in the Southeast
item.description: An invasive insect that's tough to detect and eliminate poses a multi-billion dollar threat to the agricultural economy — adding another stressor to farmers already stretched by high costs.

item.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
item.description: A new report finds generational wealth is widening the divide between homebuyers and those priced out. The median age of first-time buyers also remains at a record high.

item.title: As budgets tighten, people are breaking out their library cards
item.description: Some Americans squeezed by high prices are relying more on their local libraries for things like books, streaming services and high-priced items like musical instruments and sewing machines.

item.title: Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
item.description: A new Democratic majority in Congress could pressure the president to end the war in Iran. But it will be harder for them to directly affect fuel prices, which are tied to a complex international oil market.

item.title: Legendary photographer on getting that perfect election night picture
item.description: On election night, photographers will be in position, ready to snap history-making moments. It's something Pulitzer-prize-winner photographer David Hume Kennerly, has done for decades.

item.title: A Binance engineer thought he was interviewing for a job. Then the hackers pounced
item.description: North Korean hackers pulled off the biggest cyber heist ever by duping a Binance engineer into thinking he was being recruited for a job, the crypto exchange says.
